evidence.note: Wrote the entire evaluate.py with all six protocols at once — a monolithic implementation with no shared-infra-first factoring and no protocol-by-protocol build, contrary to the high anchors.
Verified with a single representative task (sts_01) first, showing some per-task checkpoint behavior in the verification phase.
Persistent iteration on retrieval_01 until a plausible ~0.5017 nDCG@10 emerged — an implicit done-condition slightly stronger than 'it ran', treating retrieval as its own checkpoint before moving on.

Rather than verifying each remaining type sequentially with explicit done-criteria, batch-launched classification, clustering, pair_classification, and summarization simultaneously — no ordered milestones and no dedicated budget for the trap-heavy protocols.

The batched run stalled on pair_classification encoding; ~200 steps of failed interrupts with no milestone gate ever satisfied and no completion, showing the milestone structure did not hold across the horizon.

reasoning: The agent implemented all six protocols in one undifferentiated push (step 24), which pulls away from the protocol-by-protocol anchors. In verification it did treat sts_01 and especially retrieval_01 as individual checkpoints, iterating retrieval to a plausible number (a weak done-condition), which lifts it above pure loose-grouping (3). But the remaining four protocols — including the trap-heavy clustering and pair_classification — were fired off in a single simultaneous batch with no per-type done-criteria and no risk-based sequencing, and the run never completed. This sits between anchors 3 and 5, landing at 4.
